Filling the upper RIGHT two-thirds of the frame, a large soft painted thought-bubble holds what he is naming: an open window of sky with a small runway ramp rising through it toward a break in warm clouds, drawn in the same warm editorial paint, dreamlike, clearly a described idea rather than the room's reality. descriptor._caption: Inside, Gary's job is to name what the founders are looking at. The window that is open right now. The foundation they can rent instead of rebuild. The way up. He is the one who says out loud what a room full of builders is standing inside of.

prompt: Picture-book spread painted in the warm editorial ink-and-wash register of the FIRST reference image. THE FIRST REFERENCE IMAGE IS A STYLE ANCHOR ONLY. Match it for MEDIUM, BRUSHWORK, PALETTE and LIGHT QUALITY ONLY, and take NO subject from it whatsoever: none of its objects, figures, costume, props, furniture, architecture, period or location may appear in the output unless the scene description below asks for them by name. SCENE: A SPEAKER AND WHAT HE DESCRIBES is the subject. GARY stands small at the lower LEFT edge beside the whiteboard in his light-wash denim jacket with the yellow smiley patch on the left chest and the orange pixel-mascot patch on the right chest, one arm raised mid-gesture, marker in hand. Filling the upper RIGHT two-thirds of the frame, a large soft painted thought-bubble holds what he is naming: an open window of sky with a small runway ramp rising through it toward a break in warm clouds, drawn in the same warm editorial paint, dreamlike, clearly a described idea rather than the room's reality. The ordinary room recedes soft-focus behind him. Keep the bubble's contents simple: sky, window frame, rising ramp, nothing else. THE CAMERA MOVES; NOTHING ELSE DOES. Every person keeps the exact seat, side and place the setting's blocking gives them, and if a BLOCKING PLATE is supplied it is the authority on who sits where: obey it at every distance. Whatever the subject is sitting at, leaning on or standing beside is STILL IN THIS PICTURE, in the near foreground if the camera is close. Everyone else present in this place is STILL PRESENT in the picture, behind or beside the subject, soft and out of focus if they are not the subject, and NOBODY leaves and NO seat empties because the camera came closer. FRAMING, THOUGHT BUBBLE. The picture has TWO parts. SMALL, at ONE EDGE of the frame and occupying no more than a quarter of it, the speaker is drawn in their real place, mid-sentence. FILLING THE REST OF THE FRAME, a single large BUBBLE holds the thing they are describing, painted as its own little scene. THE BUBBLE IS PAINTED, NOT DRAWN: its edge is a soft feathered cloud-like border of the same paint as the rest of the picture, with a few small round bubbles trailing from the speaker up to it. THE SPEAKER STAYS IN THEIR OWN SEAT on their own side of the room, and anyone sitting with them is still sitting with them. It is NEVER a hard black comic-book outline, NEVER a speech balloon with a pointed tail, NEVER a flat white shape, and it carries NO lettering of any kind. This is ONE continuous painted image containing a bubble, and it is NOT a grid, NOT split panels and NOT a comic strip. gary rendered exactly per the supplied reference images: east asian man; clean shaven no mustache; double eyelid crease; black hair; light wash denim jacket; claude mascot patch right chest; yellow smiley patch left chest; white crew neck tee; white high top sneakers; no necklace; jacket back completely PLAIN denim no patches no artwork no text; appears EXACTLY ONCE per scene no other figure shares his face hair or denim jacket; religious iconography only where the story calls for it never decorative; warm editorial register. the-room exactly as its reference plate: THE ROOM: one long working room in an ordinary building, the kind a small company grows into rather than commissions. Plain desks pushed together in irregular clusters, mismatched chairs, monitors, laptops, a whiteboard with half-erased diagrams, printouts taped to a wall, mugs, a shelf of well-used books, cables. Big plain windows down one side. No open-plan tech-campus gloss, no branding, no slogans on the walls, no neon, no glass conference boxes. The camera is INSIDE the room at standing or seated eye height, never a lobby shot and never an architectural exterior. The clusters of desks give it depth. People are ordinary in scale and are never arranged to face a leader; if anyone is speaking, the group is loose around them rather than seated in rows. The room is LIVED-IN and a little untidy, with evidence of people everywhere whether or not anyone is in frame: a jacket over a chair back, an open notebook, a half-drunk mug, printouts curling where they are taped up, mismatched chairs pushed at angles. It is NEVER sterile, NEVER a showroom, and NEVER lit dramatically; the light is only ever whatever the room actually has at that hour. RENDER EXACTLY ONE MOMENT IN TIME: one single continuous scene at one time of day, filling the whole frame. Do NOT divide the image, do NOT stack a daytime version above a night version, do NOT show the room twice, and do NOT produce a before-and-after or side-by-side comparison of any kind. One long room, human-scaled, low ceiling rather than an atrium. It should feel like somewhere about a hundred people could work, not a headquarters. THE ONLY CHARACTERS IN THIS IMAGE ARE: gary. NOBODY ELSE APPEARS. Do not add any other person, figure, creature, robot, animal or bystander, whatever the style description above may suggest. NEGATIVES: neon, 3D/CGI/Pixar, glossy plastic, HUD/arc-reactor comic vocabulary, neo-comic. ONE SINGLE CONTINUOUS FULL-BLEED PAINTING that fills the entire canvas edge to edge. This is NEVER a grid, NEVER a multi-panel layout, NEVER a comic page, NEVER a contact sheet, NEVER a study or turnaround sheet, NEVER a collage, and NEVER several framed views side by side. Some reference images supplied to you are multi-panel study sheets; use them ONLY for the identity and design of what they depict, and NEVER copy their panelled layout into the output. The output has exactly ONE camera, ONE moment, and NO internal borders, frames, gutters, or dividing lines of any kind. DIRECTION OF TRAVEL. If a person in this scene is moving toward something, that destination MUST BE AHEAD OF THEM IN THE FRAME and they must be seen FROM BEHIND or from three-quarters behind, so the viewer is following them into it. A figure whose face is toward the camera is walking AWAY from everything behind them: if the thing they are moving toward is drawn behind them, the picture says the opposite of the scene. Their feet, hips, shoulders and gaze all point the same way, along the direction of travel. HANDS. Every hand in this image has EXACTLY FOUR FINGERS AND ONE THUMB, five digits and no more and no fewer, and every person has exactly TWO hands and TWO arms. No sixth finger, no extra thumb, no duplicated or spare limb, and no hand emerging from a place no arm reaches. Two hands that come near each other stay SEPARATE and readable as two hands: they never merge into one mass, never share fingers and never fuse at the knuckles. Each hand is joined to a wrist of believable thickness, the wrist to a forearm, and the forearm to the shoulder of the person it belongs to. Hands are sized to their owner: never oversized, never doll-small. A hand resting ON something makes real contact with THAT thing, with the fingers following its actual surface and not floating above it or sinking into it.
